t: Section 14704 of title 40, United States Code, shall be applied to amounts made available by this joint resolution by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this joint resolution for “October 1, 2012”.

fable.w: This provision only substitutes a date in an existing statutory sunset provision for purposes of funds made available by a continuing resolution. The tempting reading is that 40 U.S.C. 14704 relates to the Appalachian Regional Commission, a federal-state body, so extending it implies participation. But the text itself sets up no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: shall be applied to amounts made available by this joint resolution by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this joint resolution for “October 1, 2012”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to an appropriations bill, merely changing a deadline date for the application of a specific statute. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or state/tribal consultations mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Section 14704 of title 40, United States Code, shall be applied to amounts made available by this joint resolution by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this joint resolution for “October 1, 2012”.

opus.w: This is a technical appropriations provision that changes a date when applying an existing statute to funds in a continuing resolution. It does not require or allow the federal government to consult anyone outside the government before making a decision. The cross-reference may point to a provision about the Appalachian Regional Commission, which has state members, but this section itself creates no outside-party process. A citation alone is not participation.
opus.s: Section 14704 of title 40, United States Code, shall be applied to amounts made available by this joint resolution by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this joint resolution for “October 1, 2012”.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that modifies the applicability date of another statute (Section 14704 of Title 40) for funds appropriated by the joint resolution. It does not create any new process for consultation, comment, or participation by outside parties. It is purely administrative and procedural regarding the timing of statutory application.
qwen_chat.s: Section 14704 of title 40, United States Code, shall be applied to amounts made available by this joint resolution by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this joint resolution for “October 1, 2012”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that applying a statute by reference could implicitly include participation mechanisms from that statute. However, this section is purely a technical amendment regarding the applicability date of a spending limitation or administrative rule. It does not itself establish any process for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a decision. It is a procedural housekeeping provision.
